title: Montana Youth Rugby Registration Analytics
headline: Turned complex Rugby Xplorer registration exports into a self-serve analytics tool that lets Montana Youth Rugby program managers track growth, retention, and reach across 8 clubs.
problem: Rugby Xplorer registration reports are complex and can't be cross-referenced across seasons or programs, so program managers had no easy way to compare clubs or see trends.

features.name: AI Overview
features.detail: Every filter change generates a plain-English summary of what the numbers mean.

features.name: Explore and Query
features.detail: Seven filters and a Breakdown view slice 2,615 registrations instantly, with CSV and PNG export.

features.name: Compare
features.detail: Any two programs, teams, or age bands side by side across seasons.

features.name: Upload and update
features.detail: New Rugby Xplorer exports drop straight in, with duplicates skipped, so the tool grows every season.

features.name: Secure by design
features.detail: Google sign-in and a de-identified default view.

insights: Statewide player registrations tripled, from 257 in 2023 to 783 in 2026.
38% of player registrations are returning players.
Missoula, Bozeman, and Helena lead, with players spread across Montana.
Gallatin Wranglers is the largest program at 21% of players, and team-level views show where individual teams peaked or declined.
result: Program managers can now see growth, retention, location, and program-level trends in one place instead of digging through raw exports.
summary: Those exports can't be cross-referenced across seasons or programs, so there was no easy way to compare clubs or see trends. Now it all lives in one place instead of raw registration files.

title: USA Rugby Match Analytics
headline: Built a match analytics platform that ties an expected points model and match stats directly to film, presented to the USA Rugby head coach and analysts.
problem: Standard match stats count events equally and don't show which moments actually swung the result.

features.name: Expected points model
features.detail: Ranks match moments by their impact on scoring expectation, and every moment opens the actual footage.

features.name: Automated match analysis
features.detail: A "why the match went this way" summary covering red zone conversion, turnovers, lineouts, and missed tackles.

features.name: Possession and momentum
features.detail: A rolling view of who controlled the ball across all 80 minutes.

features.name: Season overview
features.detail: Record, points, tries, and 11 trend metrics across an 11-match season, plus a Tier 1 benchmark.

features.name: Interactive queries
features.detail: Switch between team, player, and game views across eight match tabs, from Match Sheet to Field Maps.

features.name: Import pipeline
features.detail: New games added straight from Hudl Sportscode data.

result: Presented to the USA Rugby head coach and analyst staff.
summary: Standard match stats count events equally and don't show which moments actually swung the result, so the platform ranks each moment by its effect on the scoreline and links it to the film.
inDevelopment: Stat lines linked to video: click any stat, such as a missed tackle or a lineout, to jump to those clips for coach review.
Video analysis built directly on match film.
AI analysis being trained toward predictive models.

title: Montana Varsity Rugby Initiative
headline: Built the public proposal site for making rugby a sanctioned varsity sport in Montana high schools, used by the MHSA and athletic directors reviewing the pilot.
problem: Convincing the MHSA, athletic directors, and coaches means answering cost, safety, logistics, and demand questions in one credible place.

features.name: Interactive cost model
features.detail: Every line item expands to show its math, with $4,402.06 per school per year fully covered by MIS, so schools pay $0 for three seasons.

features.name: Season and match-day plan
features.detail: Four tournament days plus a State Championship, tied directly to the referee cost.

features.name: Statewide foundation map
features.detail: The 8 program cities, each with its roughly 50-mile reach.

features.name: Evidence and momentum
features.detail: National growth, NCAA Emerging Sport status, and Olympic and 2031 World Cup context.

features.name: Timeline and FAQ
features.detail: Answers the questions athletic directors ask about safety, girls' divisions, travel, and coaching.

features.name: Conversion
features.detail: Every call to action routes to the expression of interest form.

result: Adopted as the reference site for the MHSA and athletic directors evaluating the sanctioning pilot.
summary: Sanctioning a new sport means answering cost, safety, logistics, and demand questions in one credible place, which is exactly what the proposal site is built to do.

title: TRY Sport Website and Live Impact Tracker
headline: Built the website for TRY Rugby, a Montana Institute of Sport program working to introduce rugby to every student in the state, with a live impact tracker connected directly to the program's Google Sheet.
problem: The board, donors, and schools needed a real-time, one-glance view of how many Montana students the program has reached and how many are still waiting.

features.name: Live impact tracker
features.detail: Connected to the program's Google Sheet, so the counts and school map update automatically as schools are reached, with no manual edits.

features.name: Statewide school map
features.detail: All 812 tracked schools shown as squares, sorted by enrollment and colored by status, with the school name on hover.

features.name: Reached vs remaining
features.detail: 89,115 students reached and 62,465 still waiting, which turns the remaining gap into the funding case.

features.name: Print and PDF export
features.detail: Ready for board meetings and donor packets.

features.name: Program site
features.detail: TRY Sport and TRY Rugby pages, 8 teacher testimonials, and Donate and Bring Us to Your School calls to action.

result: Gives the MIS board, donors, and schools a real-time view of statewide progress toward reaching every Montana student.

title: Automated Interest-to-Registration Email System
headline: Built an automated system that has answered 2,000+ Montana Youth Rugby interest forms, instantly sending each family a tailored email by age band, gender, and zip code and cutting average outreach time by 90%.
problem: Families found interest forms on social media and the website, then waited on manual replies, with staff retyping schedules, costs, and registration details for each program.

features.name: Multi-channel intake
features.detail: Interest forms shared on social media and the website feed a single Google Sheet.

features.name: Rules-based routing
features.detail: A script filters each response by age band, gender, and zip code, then picks the matching email for that player's club and program.

features.name: Seasonal content
features.detail: Emails are updated each season, so families always get current schedules, costs, and events.

features.name: Conversion-focused emails
features.detail: Season blocks, training times, a cost breakdown, college pathways, a live calendar link, and a Register Online button.

result: 2,000+ interest forms answered automatically and a 90% reduction in average outreach time.
note: Built before Claude Code using early ChatGPT coding capabilities in 2025.
